news.headline: Connecticut pay transparency expansion took effect Oct 1: ads must show a wage or range plus a benefits description, and the range must be good-faith
news.why: Pay ranges are becoming mandatory in more US states, which supports our salary-up-front pitch and answers the 'we lose negotiating room' objection.
news.action: Founder posts the drafted LinkedIn reaction; check the statute before posting.

news.headline: 2026 LinkedIn Hiring Release, Wave 1: Teams collaboration for hiring managers and ATS applicants included in Hiring Assistant evaluations
news.source: LinkedIn Talent Solutions (official; release date not confirmed)
news.why: The end-game acquirer is moving into AI-assisted screening of applicants. That strengthens our 'mutual opt-in, no applicant pile' contrast.
news.action: Rizer: add to the 'why you and not LinkedIn' notes and the acquirer watch list in docs/investors.md.

news.headline: Upwork to report Q3 2026 results on November 2 (announced Oct 12)
news.why: A direct competitor for cross-border engineers shares market data on Nov 2, the same day as the YC W27 deadline.
news.action: Rizer: read the Nov 2 release for marketplace and AI-work commentary to cite (with source) in investor updates.

news.headline: Pay transparency in 2026: California SB 642 requires the posted pay scale to be a good-faith estimate, effective Jan 1, 2026
news.why: US startups hiring remote roles are exposed to state pay-range rules, so 'a real range from day one' is a practical hook for founders and CTOs.
news.action: Selly: use as a discovery question ('how do you post ranges for remote roles today?'). No legal claims in outreach.

news.headline: Maine pay transparency law signed in April 2026; sources differ on the effective date (June 29 vs July 29, 2026)
news.why: A second state on the pay-range trend; the date needs a primary source first.
news.action: Hold for a follow-up post once the date is confirmed from the state statute.
